canonical_statement: This analysis examined whether the degree of aPTT prolongation during intravenous heparin therapy after rt-PA for acute myocardial infarction was associated with infarct-related coronary artery patency.
HART enrolled 205 patients; 106 were randomized to intravenous heparin, and this report focused on the heparin group.

population.label: Patients with acute myocardial infarction randomized to the HART intravenous-heparin arm

canonical_statement: Among the 106 patients randomized to heparin, 100 had analyzable approximately 18-hour angiograms and 94 also had baseline, 8-hour, and 12-hour aPTT values available.

population.label: HART heparin-arm patients with analyzable 18-hour angiography and baseline, 8-hour, and 12-hour aPTT values

canonical_statement: Eligible patients presented within 6 hours of chest-pain onset with at least 0.1 mV ST elevation in two contiguous leads; major exclusions included severe hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, bleeding disorders, prior CABG, recent surgery or prolonged CPR, serious medical illness, pregnancy, and current oral anticoagulant therapy.

inclusion_criteria: Presentation within 6 hours of chest-pain onset
At least 0.1 mV ST elevation in two contiguous leads
exclusion_criteria: Recent surgery or prolonged cardiopulmonary resuscitation

canonical_statement: Patients received 100 mg of intravenous rt-PA as a 6 mg bolus, 54 mg during the first hour, 20 mg during the second hour, and 5 mg/h during each of the next 4 hours.

exposures.details: 6 mg bolus; 54 mg during hour 1; 20 mg during hour 2; then 5 mg/h for 4 h

canonical_statement: The heparin arm received a 5,000 IU intravenous heparin bolus followed by 1,000 IU/h, adjusted to maintain aPTT at 1.5 to 2 times control; adjunctive therapy began with rt-PA.

exposures.details: 5,000 IU bolus followed by 1,000 IU/h, adjusted to maintain aPTT at 1.5 to 2 times control

canonical_statement: In the parent HART randomization, the comparator adjunct was oral aspirin 80 mg/day; the present aPTT-patency analysis focused on the heparin arm.
Coronary artery patency was assessed 7 to 24 hours after rt-PA (mean approximately 18 hours) and again on hospital day 7; TIMI flow grade 2 or 3 was considered open and grade 0 or 1 closed.

outcome.definition: TIMI flow grade 2 or 3 was classified as open; TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 as closed.

canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes included recurrent ischemia and hemorrhagic events; hemorrhage included intracerebral hemorrhage, a >=3 g/dL hemoglobin decrease from bleeding at an identified non-CABG site, or a >=4 g/dL decrease without an identified site.

outcome.definition: Included intracerebral hemorrhage; >=3 g/dL hemoglobin decrease due to bleeding at an identified non-CABG site; or >=4 g/dL hemoglobin decrease without an identified site.

canonical_statement: aPTT was measured with Actin SS (Dade) at baseline, 8 and 12 hours after rt-PA initiation, daily thereafter, and 3 hours after any heparin infusion-rate change.

For patients assigned to heparin, the infusion rate was reduced by 50% for 2 to 3 hours before catheterization; angiograms were interpreted in a core laboratory by a single observer unaware of treatment arm or angiographic timing.

Continuous variables were reported as mean +/- SE; categorical endpoints used chi-square or two-tailed Fisher exact tests, continuous variables used two-tailed t tests, and logistic regression was used for multivariable analysis.
In the heparin group, mean aPTT was 76 +/- 4 seconds at 8 hours and 73 +/- 4 seconds at 12 hours after rt-PA initiation, significantly prolonged versus baseline (p<0.001).

canonical_statement: The study did not directly measure reocclusion; it assessed patency approximately 18 hours after therapy, and the discussion attributed lower patency with subtherapeutic aPTT to rethrombosis using evidence from prior studies.
HART did not prospectively compare alternative heparin regimens or aPTT targets, and relatively few patients had persistently subtherapeutic aPTT values.
Patients randomized to heparin did not receive aspirin, limiting direct inference about whether concomitant aspirin would modify the aPTT-patency relationship.

The authors concluded that effective heparinization helps maintain coronary artery patency after thrombolysis with rt-PA and argued that vigorous antithrombotic therapy with heparin is a necessary adjunct for fibrin-specific thrombolytic therapy.
The study reported support in part from Genentech; Judith Hsia was identified as a recipient of a Pfizer Scholars Award.
